You are studying a gene in mouse cells being grown in a laboratory. For the mouse cells to function correctly, any given cell must have six units of functional protein encoded by your gene of interest. In heterozygous mouse cells carrying one null allele and one wild-type allele of this gene, only four protein units are produced. This gene is thus:
A lethal allele with 100% lethality for a gene interferes with laying down the basic body plan of organs in the embryonic stage of an organism. This is an example of
choices: gene interaction in a developmental pathway.
a mutant allele acting as a suppressor.

questions.text: A researcher has crossed two dihybrid plants with purple-colored flowers with the genotype  a + / a  ;  z + / z . The mutant  a / a  gives white flowers, while the mutant  zz  gives pink flowers. The progeny of this cross has the phenotypic ratio of 9 purple: 3 pink: 4 white. What type of gene interaction do these results suggest?
choices: The two genes do not interact in any way.
The two genes act in the same pathway.

questions.text: The testcross is a useful tool for \_\_\_\_\_, where the phenotypes and genotypes of gametes cannot be observed directly.
A genetic engineer deletes a few nucleotides from the genome of the blue sea star, causing its  color  to change to yellow. What has happened to the sea star\'s DNA?
choices: It has learned to camouflage itself.
A new species has been created.

questions.text: A diploid yeast cell is heterozygous for a wild-type allele and a recessive lethal allele. Upon meiosis, which of these is the expected result for the haploid meiotic progeny?
choices: Four viable progeny, but two must be temperature-sensitive

questions.text: You want to determine whether short wings in fruit flies are the result of a dominant or recessive mutation. You cross a short-winged fly stock with a long-winged fly stock (which is considered to be wild type or +/+). The progeny have a 1:1 ratio of short to long wings. You then allow the F1 short-winged flies to mate. The F2 progeny have a phenotypic ratio of 3:1 short to long wings. Short wings are likely the result of:
choices: either a dominant or a recessive mutation; additional crosses are necessary.
no mutations at all; this phenotype is likely the result of environmental factors.

questions.text: In the fungus Neurospora, a mutant has a slow-growth phenotype, called poky. If you cross the poky female with a wild-type male, all progeny are poky, but if you cross the wild-type female with the poky male, all progeny are wild type. Diagnose the inheritance pattern in these crosses.
choices: It is an autosomal dominant inheritance.
It is an autosomal recessive inheritance.

questions.text: Which statement is FALSE regarding the cytoplasmic segregation process?
choices: Alleles on organelle chromosomes in asexual cells cannot show cytoplasmic segregation.
In chloroplasts, it is a common mechanism for producing variegated plants.
Cytoplasmic segregation is not a mitotic process.
In cytohets, a type of cytoplasmic segregation can be detected.

questions.text: The recombinant genotypes from a testcross of a dihybrid in cis conformation (i.e., AB/ab) would be \_\_\_\_\_, represented as gametic classes.
If a medical disorder runs in the family, a pedigree analysis can be undertaken to predict:
choices: what other disorders are likely to occur in that family.
the probability that a certain disorder will affect the offspring of a couple in that family.
how many more propositi will occur in the family.

questions.text: Susan has MERRF (myoclonic epilepsy with ragged red  fibers ), a mitochondrial disease. She gives birth to two boys and a girl. Which of these choices is completely true?
choices: Only the daughter will inherit MERRF.
Susan inherited MERRF from her mother and will pass it down to both her male and female children.
Susan\'s grandchildren will all inherit MERRF.
None of Susan\'s children will inherit MERRF.
